subject: int vs. long vs. long long / signed vs. unsigned

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: int vs. long vs. long long / signed vs. unsigned
parts:
We hit another snag in the discrete
distributions. Right now, we have the
moral equivalent (modulo templates) of:

double poisson_log(unsigned int, double lambda);

The problem is that if someone passes an int
into this, it'll get converted to an unsigned int
and we'll never catch problems arising from it
being negative.

I propose changing all our distributions to take
a signed long and do the checks.

Anyone see any problems with that?

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] int vs. long vs. long long / signed vs. unsigned
parts:
It turns out long is typically 32 bits on
Windows (at least 32-bit versions). Here's
a nice clarification:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/589575/size-of-int-long-etc

So I'm thinking we should use

int_fast64_t

as the type of integer parameters or outcomes.

- Bob
